correctness.rationale: The grouped Poisson marks yield an exact positive \(\alpha\)-stable Laplace law for the tail with scale equal to the residual atom probability; finite \(q<\alpha\) moments and geometric tail make Markov probabilities summable. Borel–Cantelli supplies an almost-sure exponential length tail. The finite n-generator zonotope has at most \(O(n^{d-1})\) support vertices by the central hyperplane arrangement bound. Every exposed point lies within the tail length of one such vertex. Straszewicz and finite CLOSED ball unions correctly extend the covering to all extreme points, implying zero upper box, packing and Hausdorff dimensions with \(N_r=O((\log(1/r))^{d-1})\). Strict positivity of each atom-group length gives interior from d independent directions; density and strict sign separation make the exposed-point map injective on a continuum of good normals. All quantifiers, dimensions, metric balls and stability ranges are explicit. No computational or other unproved infinite-step assumptions are used.

value.rationale: Anisotropic fractal dimension and minimal spectral regularity are specifically motivated by the August 2026 theorem. This all-dimensional, almost-sure structural counterexample separates full topological support and continuum exposed complexity from any positive metric dimension. A robust class of geometric mass-tail laws and a quantitative polylogarithmic entropy estimate go beyond finite-atom polytope degeneracy and provide a benchmark and boundary case for future anisotropic and packing-dimension results. No general theorem on arbitrary distributions or optimal gauge is claimed.
